title: General Moelner: the secret craft filled a reconnaissance gap until spy satellites took over

tellings.quote: General Moelner's advice at face value, uh this thing just filled a gap. And when it had done its job of filling the gap, they went back to spy satellites.

plain: A secret American aircraft was built only to fill a gap in spying from the air, and once it had done that job the military went back to using spy satellites. That is the account of a general named General Moelner, as passed on by the aviation journalist Nick Cook, who says he takes the general's advice at face value. If true, it would explain why such a craft could be built and then quietly retired.
